text:
Cole Sillinger finally scored again on Nov. 25 against New Jersey, his first goal in ten games per RotoWire, and it was the right kind: an open look off a defensive-zone turnover. The Columbus native has 10 points in 23 games, and none of them on the power play.

The drought wasn't really about him. His own finishing is right on his chances (5 goals on 5.1 expected), but the Blue Jackets have scored about 4.8 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him assists. That kind of gap usually swings back. The bigger question is the two-way play: Columbus gets under 47% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey noted last season that strong linemates were flattering his raw numbers.

His physical game is steady, 55 hits already. That same Nov. 25 game also brought a hit that injured Denton Mateychuk, which Sillinger and Rick Bowness both addressed afterward in the Columbus Dispatch's video. Watch whether the goal opens things up.
